In an age past, the Flora were made by the God of Recursion to seek [to spread distinctive patterns throughout the land](https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/757875). At that time, Umbralocht has [lent these patterns an obsessive allure](https://voat.co/v/SavageGods/comments/757875/3723473): The Flora would be compelled to spread them throughout the world. Umbralocht saw in this a potential for conflict, as the Flora seek to expand their strange symbols where other races would not have them.

Finally, in the Age of Strife, this is coming to pass.

To the ore-mines of the Holnareem, the Flora send delegations.

To the trading posts of the Schrykes, they send expeditions.

To the gardens of the Saen, they send surveyors.

To the bountiful Forest of Brotherhood, they send explorers.

To the holy places of conteplation of the Med'ja Hom, they send migrants.

Everywhere, they test the borders, as the places easily accessible to them have already become full of recursive crystalline patterns. At some of those borders, some of those peoples would not let the Flora deface their lands so easily. Tensions mount. But the Flora would not be deterred. The Flora have machines. The Flora have numbers and population. The Flora have resources. The Floran homelands are protected by unbeatable guardians. They have nothing to fear, and so, in their arrogance, they press.

Many races of the world have concerns. There is nothing good about these strange symbols the Flora insist on carving, and many things sinister. Besides, what of holy places! Sanctums! Burial mounds! Places that must not be breached - but the Flora insist on breaching regardless. And further, how is it at all politically sensible to allow these Flora free access to roam as they please? Them and their strange machines and stranger obsessions.

Which land, which people, would resist them first? Which would submit to have their lands be carved into odd shapes? A neutral stance is no longer possible: Each race is given, in their turn, an ultimatum. It is not always so unkindly shaped; Perhaps it's backed by trade concessions, or gifts, or promises of alliance, but beneath every overture of contact, lies a promise, a threat.

Through peace or through force, your lands will be carved. Submit, or be forced. Choose.
